findings.evidence: Fig. 6.1 workload box text: 'Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency'. Same-page caption: 'Label caveat: a concurrency entry in the workload box denotes the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not a concurrency value'. Ch. 6 §6.1.1 (PDF p.142): 'Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer.'
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption / taxonomy defect: the workload box is literally labelled 'concurrency', which §6.1.1 declares is NOT a workload metric, and the caption must therefore explain that the entry 'denotes the request rate λ ... not a concurrency value'. The drawn label is wrong by the book's own three-layer taxonomy; 'rps' is already printed in the same box, so the entry is both prohibited and redundant.
findings.fix_instruction: In Fig. 6.1 (PDF p.144) relabel the workload-box entry as 'request rate λ (rps)' or delete it, then delete the 'Label caveat' sentence from the caption and the 'a concurrency entry that denotes the request rate λ' clause from §6.1.1 (PDF p.142).

findings.evidence: Fig. 6.2 in-figure legend text: 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Same-page caption: 'the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget'. Ch. 4 (PDF p.70): 'The 1.2 s and ~25 ms values are design budgets, not the pass/fail SLO thresholds. Pass/fail on a measured distribution is judged against the p95 ceilings (TTFT ≤ 2 s, TPOT ≤ 35 ms)'.
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption contradiction on a load-bearing distinction the book makes repeatedly: the drawn line is labelled 'TTFT budget' while the caption, Ch. 4 and the Canonical Workload box all state that 1.2 s is the budget and 2 s is only the p95 ceiling. A reader of the figure alone learns the opposite of the book's convention.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the Fig. 6.2 legend label (PDF p.147) from 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)' to 'SLO p95 ceiling 2 s', and remove the now-redundant 'not the 1.2 s design budget' clause from the caption.

findings.evidence: Prose (PDF p.121): 'with a 1% straggler cluster at 5.0 s [ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic mixture]'. Captions: Fig. 6.2 (PDF p.147) '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]'; Fig. 4.1 (PDF p.118), Fig. 5.1 (PDF p.141), Fig. 6.1 (PDF p.144) and List of Figures entries (PDF pp.8–9) '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]'. Preface rule (PDF p.20): 'A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes'; 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED])'. Contrast with correctly paired captions: PDF p.34 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', PDF p.35 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]', PDF p.54 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', PDF p.168 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'.
findings.issue: Malformed evidence-label pairs: an Axis-1 provenance tag is followed by a free-text word ('conceptual', 'synthetic mixture', 'synthetic profile') instead of an Axis-2 value (FACT/DERIVED/ASSUMPTION/HYPOTHESIS/UNRESOLVED). The p.121 instance is the strongest case — it labels the quantitative inputs (median 0.8 s, σ, 1% at 5.0 s, N=10,000) that drive every subsequent percentile and mean computation, so by the Preface's own rule it must be [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], and the computed percentiles must be [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The same deviation appears in four figure captions and two List of Figures entries while every other figure caption in the book uses a correct pair.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic mixture]' (PDF p.121) with '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]' for inputs and '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' for the computed percentiles; replace '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]' (Fig. 6.2, p.147) and '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' (Figs. 4.1, 5.1, 6.1 at pp.118, 141, 144, plus List of Figures pp.8–9) with the appropriate Axis-2 tag, moving any descriptive word outside the brackets.

findings.evidence: PDF p.153 (§6.3.4): '~18.6× oversubscribed (the datasheet-peak ~7.9 PFLOPS gives ~6.5×, the theoretical ceiling only; under case (ii), full-square attention, the same peak screens at ~22 hosts — Ch 8 §3), consistent with Ch 8's 19-host screen at this peak (case (i))'.
findings.issue: Ambiguous referent producing two different host counts. The immediately preceding noun phrase is 'datasheet-peak ~7.9 PFLOPS', so 'the same peak' naturally binds to the capacity ceiling; under that reading case (ii) demand 40 × 1.51 ≈ 60.4 PFLOP/s ÷ 7.9 PFLOPS = 7.65 → 8 hosts, contradicting the stated 22. The intended referent is the 40 rps traffic peak at the same 35% MFU planning rate (60.4 ÷ 2.77 = 21.8 → 22), recoverable only from 'at this peak' two clauses later.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the parenthetical on PDF p.153 to name both quantities explicitly: '(the datasheet-peak ~7.9 PFLOPS gives ~6.5×, a theoretical ceiling only; under case (ii), full-square attention, the same 40 rps traffic peak at the same 35% MFU planning rate screens ~22 hosts — Ch 8 §3)'.

findings.evidence: Page 132 (§6.8): "Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21. That is the capacity floor, which is the max of the named screens, not the prefill compute screen alone: case (i)'s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little's-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds (Ch 8 §3; Ch 17)."
findings.issue: The mini-case's own arithmetic contains a contradiction the text does not flag: it computes the fleet oversubscription as 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H and then, two paragraphs earlier, says the 40 rps peak "demands 40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s ≈ 18.6 host-equivalents" for a single host — but 51.6 ÷ 2.77 = 18.6, so 18.6 is the SINGLE-HOST requirement (H = 1), while the text then reads "the fleet oversubscription at peak is 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H" and concludes "on the single host this mini-case assumes ... that is a ~4.7× oversubscription at baseline and 18.6× at the peak". The prefill screen for the fleet is then given as "⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts", i.e. the single-host-equivalent figure is used as the fleet host count without the reader being told that 18.6 is already a host-equivalent count (18.6 hosts needed), not an oversubscription ratio that must be divided by H again. The ratio and the absolute count are the same number used in two roles (an oversubscription factor at H=1 and a host count at fleet level), which is exactly the unit conflation the chapter elsewhere warns against.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the mini-case's prefill arithmetic to keep the two roles separate: state the peak prefill demand as 51.6 PFLOP/s, the single-host sustained capacity as 2.77 PFLOP/s, the host-equivalent requirement as 51.6 ÷ 2.77 ≈ 18.6 hosts, and the oversubscription at H hosts as 18.6/H — then take the prefill screen as ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts explicitly as a host count (not a factor), and state that the KV-residency screen's 21 hosts is the binding one.

findings.evidence: Page 132 (§6.8): "Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21. ... At 21 hosts the 344 in-flight peak requests fit the 21 × 17 = 357 resident slots, and the peak prefill oversubscription falls from 18.6× to 51.6 ÷ (21 × 2.77) ≈ 0.9× (measured against the 21-host prefill capacity and before any cache saving; the ≤ 13% prefix-cache reduction can only lower it, so 0.9× is an upper bound on the post-cache ratio at this host count)"
findings.issue: The mini-case asserts a definite fleet size (21 hosts) and a fleet-level resolution ("p95 TTFT is back under 2 s") while the same chapter repeatedly states that these screens are not capacity results — e.g. p. 155 (§6.8, earlier paragraph): "That is the capacity floor, which is the max of the named screens" and Ch. 4 p. 116: "These are analytical screens on the planning basis, not capacity results — Ch. 17 recomputes them." The mini-case therefore reports a production fleet size and an SLO restoration as a conclusion of the narrative when the arithmetic it cites supports only an analytical screen; the label discipline the book applies elsewhere (ANALYTICAL / SCENARIO-DERIVED, not measured) is absent on this sentence, and the p. 155 text already flags "goodput restoration is expected but not claimed here" — leaving the reader with an unexplained asymmetry between the p95 claim (asserted) and the goodput claim (withheld).
findings.fix_instruction: Attach the book's measurement-status vocabulary to the mini-case's fleet conclusion — e.g. mark 21 hosts as an ANALYTICAL screen and state that the p95 TTFT restoration is a hypothesis pending benchmark confirmation (Ch. 14/Ch. 17), matching how the same host count is labelled in Ch. 4 §4.6 and Ch. 17.
